pattern_id: EPaxos recovery drops conflicting dependency when merging PREACCEPTED views
description: In a 3-node EPaxos cluster (R0,R1,R2), command op1 (I1 = (R0,0)) is fast-committed on {R0,R1} while R2 never sees it. Later, op2 (I2 = (R2,0)) is proposed at R2. R2’s local PreAccept for I2 has seq=1, deps=∅ because it is unaware of I1. R2 sends PreAccept(I2) to R0 and R1, but only R1 receives it. R1 has committed I1 on the same key, so it PreAccepts I2 with seq=2 and deps including I1, and persists this PREACCEPTED state. The reply from R1 to R2 is lost, so R2 times out and starts EPaxos recovery for I2. During recovery, R2 sends Prepare(I2) to R0 and R1. R0 replies with Status=NONE (it never saw I2), while R1 replies Status=PREACCEPTED with (seq=2, deps={I1}). The correct algorithm must adopt a value/metadata that is at least as strong as any PREACCEPTED/ACCEPTED report, preserving the dependency on I1. However, in this implementation handlePrepareReply always initializes recoveryInst from the local PREACCEPTED view when startRecoveryForInstance runs, and later PREACCEPTED replies that disagree in (Seq,Deps) do not override that recoveryInst. As a result, the recovery leader keeps its local seq=1,deps=∅ for I2, and bcasts Commit(I2) with no dependency on I1. All replicas then install I2 with deps missing I1 via handleCommit. Executing I2 followed by I1 yields final k=1 instead of k=2, violating agreement on both dependency graph and application state.
trigger_condition: 1) Fast-path commit of a conflicting instance I1 that is unseen by at least one replica. 2) A second conflicting instance I2 is started at that replica and seen (PreAccepted) by some other replica that knows I1, which sets deps(I2) to include I1. 3) The PreAccept reply with elevated seq/deps is lost so the leader of I2 only stores its local, weaker PREACCEPTED view. 4) The leader crashes or times out and initiates recovery. 5) During recovery it receives Prepare replies: NONE from one replica and PREACCEPTED with stronger dependencies from another. 6) The recovery logic keeps the original local (Seq,Deps) and never updates recoveryInst from the richer PREACCEPTED reply, then drives I2 to Commit with the truncated dependency set.
test_template: Set up an in-memory EPaxos cluster (using a helper like CrashReuseReplica or equivalent). Install a committed instance I1=(p,0) with a PUT on key k at a subset of replicas, leaving at least one replica unaware. Then install PREACCEPTED views for a conflicting instance I2=(q,0): at the recovering replica q, seq=1,deps=∅; at a second replica, seq>1 and deps including I1. Call startRecoveryForInstance(q,0) at replica q, then manually construct and feed PrepareReply messages into handlePrepareReply: one NONE reply from a replica that does not know I2, one PREACCEPTED reply from the replica with deps including I1. After handlePrepareReply drives the instance out of preparing (into ACCEPTED or a new Phase1), construct a Commit for I2 using the recovered metadata and deliver it to all replicas via handleCommit. Finally, deliver Commit(I1) to all replicas and assert: (a) deps(I2) includes I1 and seq(I2)≥seq(I1) at every replica; (b) executing I2 then I1 at each replica via the exec engine yields identical final state (e.g., key k==2). An implementation that loses the dependency will produce deps(I2) missing I1 and final state k==1, causing the test to fail and revealing the bug.
